correctness.rationale: For n>=2 and 0<r≠s, angular DFT decomposes the Gram of two aligned regular n-gons of normalized Gaussian coherent kernels into 2x2 Hermitian blocks indexed ell. The two residue-supported Fock coefficient sequences are nonproportional when r≠s; all blocks are strictly positive. At s=r+epsilon the small block eigenvalue is (epsilon²/2)||P_{v}^perp v'_ell||²+O(|epsilon|³). Component logarithmic derivative k/r−r identifies the squared residual as Lambda_ell(r²) Var(Poisson(r²)|k≡ell mod n)/r². The small-r first-two-terms argument gives unique ell=n−1 and c_n(r)~n³r^{4n−4}/[2(2n−1)!]. The exact roots-of-unity expression Lambda_ell(t)=sum_j omega^{-j ell} exp[t(omega^j−1)] gives c_ell(sqrt t)=1/2+|omega−1|²t exp[−(1−cos theta)t] cos(sin(theta)t−ell theta+phi)+o(t exp[−gamma t]) for fixed n>=3. At the prescribed phase sequence each ell uniquely minimizes infinitely often; uniform little-oh over finite sectors makes this rigorous. Independently evaluated the derivative root filter at late phase-selected t for n=3,4,6, obtaining each predicted minimizer; finite checks do not establish infinitely many radii.
